_comment: Enrollment manifest for the CI test gates. Every workspace that pnpm-workspace.yaml
resolves must appear here — either with a floor under `vitest.workspaces`, or with a
written reason under `vitest.exempt`. A workspace that exists on disk and is missing
from both fails the gate, so adding a package without adding tests is a red build
rather than a global count that silently absorbs the gap.
Floors are per project, not global: a package that stops contributing tests entirely
cannot hide behind its neighbours' counts. Raising a floor is a normal part of adding
tests; lowering one is a decision that shows up in review — see `ratchet` below, and
scripts/ci/assert-floor-ratchet.mjs, which compares every number here against the same
file on origin/main.
Floors sit a little under the real counts on purpose. They are a loss detector, not a
target: the point is to catch a suite that shrank, not to go red every time a test is
renamed away. Counted from a real run of this tree (fix/ci-r6 merged into fix/auth-r5,
plus #40): core 129, db 23, auth 220, ingest 150, server 104, web 16, ci-guard 124 — 766
tests across 31 files. Round 7 took ci-guard from 49 to 124: the outside witness now
tests the *behaviour* of every shared decision under scripts/ci/, not only the shape of
the guard in its callers — see scripts/ci/checker-graph.mjs. Its floor moved 40 -> 115,
because a floor a few under a real count is a loss detector and one 84 under it
is a place seventy tests can be deleted from.
packages/ci-guard is #40 round 6. It exists to run checks from *outside* scripts/: the
main-module guard scanner was enforced only from gate-selftest.mjs, a file it scans, so
one `&&` in that file removed 316 assertions with every gate green. Its floor is what
makes deleting those tests loud — see scripts/ci/checker-graph.mjs, which requires every
enforcement check to have a witness that is not one of its own subjects, and requires that
witness to assert on the result rather than merely call it.
apps/web left `exempt` and acquired a floor in #40's merge: fix/auth-r5 gave it a Vitest
project for its server-side modules (the boot conditions in `lib/env.ts`, and #40's
rules about build-time constants in `next.config.ts`), which a browser suite cannot
reach. Its Playwright suite is still the `playwright` section below.

Round 9 took ci-guard from 115 to 150: the outside witness now also covers the deployment precondition, the mail relay address, the report gates' exit status, the identity-vs-behaviour rule over control expectations, the assertion floors, and the round-4 entry decision over the whole repository — 160 tests as measured. And it added `assertions.scripts` below, which is a second kind of floor entirely: see the comment there.

Round 10 took ci-guard from 150 to 180: the outside witness now also covers the two-world measurement behind the deployment precondition, the generated corpus of reds a control did not plant, the runtime assertion and request floors, the rule that a recorded assertion must read a value, and the resolution-based reading of this repository's entry points out of a workflow — 188 tests as measured, 830 across the workspace.
Floors ratchet up. scripts/ci/assert-floor-ratchet.mjs reads this same file from
origin/main and fails if any floor here is lower than the one there — including the
quiet version, where an enrolled workspace is moved into `exempt` instead.
A decrease is allowed with a written reason keyed to exactly what came down, e.g.
"vitest.workspaces.packages/core.minTests": "why the suite is legitimately smaller".
Justifications are checked in both directions: one that does not match an actual
decrease fails too, so nobody can pre-authorise next month's cut by landing a blanket
reason today.
There is no baseline until this branch merges — origin/main carries no manifest yet —
so today the script says `no baseline` loudly and checks only that every floor is a
whole number of at least 1. It becomes a real ratchet the moment a manifest exists on
main.
Floors on how many assertions each stack assertion still records, added in #40 round 9 and given a runtime half in round 10.

The positive control in scripts/ci/positive-control.mjs proves a script is a function of the deployment by running it where there is none. That catches a script that checks nothing; it cannot catch one cut down to its `requireDeployment` precondition, which goes red in that world exactly like the real thing.

`minChecks` is the round-9 half: how many `check(…)` call sites the source holds, counted by scripts/ci/checker-graph.mjs from the imports rather than from this table, so a script that starts recording assertions and has no floor is an error and a floor for a script that stopped is an error too.

`minRun` is the round-10 half, and it exists because a floor over a loop is a floor over nothing. Four scripts record every problem through ONE call site over a computed list — `for (const problem of problems) check(false, problem)` — so their source floor was 1, and a blind critic replaced the main block of assert-stack-schema.mjs (529 lines) with an empty list and measured `assert-stack-schema: passed.` against the live migrated stack: red cold, green hot, floor satisfied, zero schema compared. `minRun` is the count the RUN reports — `check(…)` plus whatever `compared(n, …)` records for comparisons that found nothing wrong — and `verdict` in scripts/ci/stack-client.mjs enforces it against the live deployment. The number comes from inside the comparison (checkSchema returns how many tables, columns, constraints and indexes it examined), so a rewrite that skips the comparison cannot report having made it.

`minRequests` is the third dimension and the one a tautology cannot fake: how many questions the script actually put to the deployment through `once(…)`. Round 10's D3 exploit was twenty-three `check(true, …)` calls after the precondition, which satisfies any count of assertions and asks the deployment exactly one thing.
These sit in `floorsOf`, so assert-floor-ratchet.mjs ratchets them against origin/main like every test floor, and the README's floors fingerprint moves when one of them does.

Measured against a live stack on this tree, and set a little under: preflight 18, image-identity 3, image-origins 589, migration-image 3, page-serves 29 with 25 requests, rate-limit 7, signup-verifies 15 with 8, stack-config 17, stack-health 45, stack-schema 260, teardown 3, ws-upgrade 9 with 8. This is a loss detector, not a target.
